newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh vows to end child labour in textiles.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh vows to end child labour in textiles.

text.p: Bangladesh's clothes exporters vowed on Sunday to end child labour in the textiles industry.

"We have made it clear to foreign buyers that our factories would be free of child labour by October," Redwan Ahmed, chief of the Bangladesh garment association, told a news conference at the end of a three-day textile fair in Dhaka on Sunday.
"We told them that now they can buy apparels with a free mind and conscience," he added.
Ahemd said the fair was aimed at attracting new buyers for the country's textile products which account for 65 percent of export earnings in Bangladesh.

Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, the International Labour Organisation (ILO) and the United Nations Children Fund (UNICEF) are rehabilitating more than 10,500 child workers under a July 1995 agreement.
Clothes makers agreed to the terms after the United States, a big importer of Bangladeshi garments, threatened to stop buying textiles from nations using workers below the age of 14.
Under a pact reached with the ILO and UNICEF, 130 schools for child labourers were set up and 2,015 students enrolled. Besides schooling, children also receive stipends.
Redwan said 370 foreign buyers visited the exhibition and made spot orders amounting to $32 million.

"Business worth $300 million is expected in the next three months. Buyers' responses were encouraging," he said. The country earned about $2.5 billion from clothes exports in the year up to June 1996.
